assumptions: Fluid treated as slightly compressible; density error ~ Ma^2 must stay <~1% (Ma = v_max/c0 <= 0.1)
Inviscid in the dam-break benchmark; artificial viscosity supplies dissipation and stability
Free surface needs no explicit BC (pressure clamped >= 0 or negative pressures allowed per scheme); summation density underestimates near surface
Equal particle masses m = rho0 * dx^2 (2D)
methods.discretization: Lagrangian particles on initial lattice spacing dx; kernel support 2h with h = 1.2-1.3 dx (PySPH dam_break_2d: hdx=1.3, Wendland quintic); explicit time integration (PySPH: predict-evaluate-correct, WCSPH; symplectic/leapfrog also common).
methods.boundary_conditions: Solid walls: layers of fixed boundary particles (PySPH dam_break_2d: 2 layers, whose density is evolved/EOS-computed - dynamic boundary particles as in Gomez-Gesteira 2010) or repulsive forces (Monaghan 1994, not verified). Free surface: implicit. Taylor-Green: periodic, no walls.
methods.stability: c0 >= 10 Umax (Umax ~ sqrt(2 g H) for dam break; PySPH uses c0 = 10*sqrt(2*9.81*2) = 62.6 m/s for H = 2 m). Acoustic CFL: PySPH dam_break_2d dt = 0.125 h/c0 (with adaptive_timestep); taylor_green dt = min(0.25 h/(c0+U), 0.125 h^2/nu). EDAC manuscript: dt = min(h/(4(c_s+|U|max)), h^2/(8 nu)). Force condition dt <= 0.25 sqrt(h/|f|max) (Becker & Teschner via secondary, unverified).

assumptions: Incompressibility enforced as position constraints solved by a few Jacobi iterations per step (not converged: residual density error remains)
Velocity derived from position change v = (x* - x)/dt (first-order); damping from XSPH; energy loss partly restored by vorticity confinement
Equal masses; density computed with poly6, gradients with spiky kernel
Graphics method: no physical sound speed; viscosity is numerical, not a Reynolds-number model
methods.discretization: Predict x* = x + dt(v + dt f_ext); neighbour search; for iter in 1..N: compute lambda_i, Delta p_i (with s_corr), collision/boundary projection, x* += Delta p; v = (x*-x)/dt; apply vorticity confinement + XSPH; x = x*. Taichi pbf2d: 5 iterations, dt = 1/20 in its scaled units; Macklin reports 2-4 iterations typical (unverified).
methods.boundary_conditions: Walls handled by clamping/projecting predicted positions into the domain (taichi-pbf2d confine_position_to_boundary with tiny random jitter); boundary particles optional (Akinci-style in SPlisHSPlasH).
methods.stability: Unconditionally stable in the PBD sense (positions projected), but accuracy degrades with large dt: compression grows if iterations are too few. Keep max displacement per step < ~h/2 (common practice, not from the paper). epsilon (CFM relaxation) prevents division by zero for isolated particles.

assumptions: Weakly compressible, inviscid fluid; only the scalar volume ratio J is tracked (no deviatoric stress)
Particles carry mass, velocity, affine matrix C (APIC) and J; grid is a scratch-pad rebuilt each step
MLS shape-function gradient replaced by the APIC/MLS affine form so no kernel gradients are needed (Hu et al. 2018 main claim)
methods.discretization: Uniform background grid n_grid^2 on [0,1]^2 (mpm88: 128^2, dx=1/128), ~4 particles per cell initially (p_vol=(dx/2)^2), explicit symplectic-Euler style step P2G -> grid update -> G2P.
methods.boundary_conditions: Grid-node velocity: outward normal component set to zero within `bound` = 3 cells of each wall (separating slip). mls-mpm88-cpp uses sticky walls on 3 sides and separating floor.
methods.stability: Explicit; dt limited by CFL on grid with sound speed: dt <= C dx/(|v|max + c), c = sqrt(E/rho). mpm88: c = sqrt(400/1) = 20, dt*c/dx = 2e-4*20*128 = 0.51 (derived here, not stated in source). Particles must not leave the 3x3 stencil: |v| dt < dx.

scenes.setup: Column width a, height 2a (n^2 = 2), dry horizontal floor, wall at x=0 behind the column, released at t=0. Martin & Moyce: a = 2.25 in (57.15 mm) and 1.125 in; Lethe: a=3.5, g=1; PySPH (Gomez-Gesteira 2010 setup): a=1 m, H=2 m, tank 4 m x 4 m, g=9.81.
scenes.conventions: Z = x_front/a, T = t*sqrt(2g/a) (Martin & Moyce, PySPH, Lethe). T_K = t*sqrt(g/a) = T/sqrt(2). T_H = t*sqrt(g/H) with H=2a equals T/2. Front taken as max x of fluid particles (PySPH) or max x with phase>0.5 (Lethe).
scenes.tolerance: max |Z_sim - Z_ref| <= 0.25 for T in (0,3] after allowing one time shift dT in [0,0.25] (Lethe applies +0.175); report shift. Late time compare to a225 series up to tank end.
scenes.cross_check: Lethe copy vs PySPH mm_data_2 (both a=2.25 in): |dZ| = 0.011, 0.006, 0.065, 0.079 at T = 0.83, 1.22, 2.00, 2.55. PySPH mm_data_1 (a=1.125 in) vs Lethe: |dZ| <= 0.074. PySPH ko_data vs Lethe: up to 0.31 (T=2.72).

scenes.setup_sph: Unit periodic box, u=-U e^{bt}cos(2 pi x)sin(2 pi y), v=U e^{bt}sin(2 pi x)cos(2 pi y), p=-U^2 e^{2bt}(cos 4 pi x+cos 4 pi y)/4, b=-8 pi^2/Re, Re=100, U=1, c0=10U, nx=50 (PySPH default), quintic spline, h=dx (EDAC) or hdx*dx.
findings: Kinetic energy decays as exp(2bt) = exp(-16 pi^2 t/Re) for this normalisation (from exact solution, pysph-tg)
Uniform (unperturbed) initial lattice gives ~10x larger error than relaxed init in Adami 2013 (as reported by ramachandran2019edac); EDAC uses random perturbation of max dx/5
EDAC(TVF) L1 velocity error ~4x below TVF at nx=50, Re=100 (ramachandran2019edac text)
Standard WCSPH is the worst of the compared schemes on TG (ramachandran2019edac Fig. tgv:l1_error, qualitative)
Classical WCSPH/TVF do not converge with resolution at Re=100 (negi2022convergence; ramachandran2019edac)
